title: Superposition and Wave Function Collapse
text:
In quantum mechanics, the principle of superposition dictates that a physical system exists in all possible states simultaneously until it is measured. This allows particles, such as electrons, to occupy multiple locations or possess multiple spins at once, represented by a mathematical wave function.

The act of measurement forces the wave function to collapse instantaneously. Upon observation, the particle's state resolves into a single, definite outcome—a process that fundamentally links measurement to reality definition within quantum theory.

Furthermore, entanglement describes a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same existence, regardless of the physical distance separating them. Measuring the property of one entangled particle instantaneously determines the corresponding property of the other, suggesting non-local correlations beyond classical understanding.
